subproblem.title: Smooth cutoff equal to 1 on B_rho(y), supported in B_{2rho}(y), with gradient at most K/rho
subproblem.statement: There is a real constant K >= 0 such that for every natural number n, every point y in R^n (Rn n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)) and every rho > 0 there is a function eta : R^n -> R with: eta is C^1 on R^n; 0 <= eta(x) <= 1 for every x; eta(x) = 1 for every x in the open ball B_rho(y); eta has compact support; the topological support tsupport(eta) is contained in the open ball B_{2 rho}(y); and ||D eta(x)|| <= K / rho for every x in R^n, where D eta(x) = fderiv R eta x and ||.|| is the operator norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∃ K : ℝ, 0 ≤ K ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (y : Rn n) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ∃ η : Rn n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 η ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ η x ∧ η x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x ∈ ball y ρ, η x = 1) ∧ HasCompactSupport η ∧ tsupport η ⊆ ball y (2 * ρ) ∧ ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ η x‖ ≤ K / ρ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 2 of the parent proof (Caccioppoli inequality for constant coefficients), where the cutoff eta(x) = psi(|x - y|^2 / rho^2) is built from Mathlib's Real.smoothTransition. The parent proof uses this cutoff with K = 4 c_psi; here its properties are proved for arbitrary n, y and rho > 0, with K independent of n, y and rho.
Notation. R^n = Rn n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) with the Euclidean norm. B_r(y) is the open ball. D eta(x) = fderiv R eta x is a linear form on R^n, and ||D eta(x)|| is its operator norm. S := Real.smoothTransition : R -> R is C^infinity and takes values in [0, 1]. It satisfies S(t) = 0 for t <= 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos) and S(t) = 1 for t >= 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le).
1. The profile. Put psi(s) := S((3 - s)/2). psi is C^infinity, in particular C^1, because S is C^infinity and s -> (3 - s)/2 is affine. Also 0 <= psi <= 1. If s <= 1 then (3 - s)/2 >= 1, so psi(s) = 1. If s >= 3 then (3 - s)/2 <= 0, so psi(s) = 0.
2. The constant. psi' is continuous because psi is C^1. If s < 1, psi equals 1 on the open neighbourhood (-infinity, 1) of s, so psi'(s) = 0. If s > 3, psi equals 0 on the open neighbourhood (3, infinity) of s, so psi'(s) = 0. Hence psi' vanishes outside [1, 3]. On the compact interval [1, 3] the continuous function |psi'| is bounded by some C_0. Put c_psi := max(C_0, 0). Then c_psi >= 0 and |psi'(s)| <= c_psi for every real s. Put K := 4 c_psi >= 0. K is a fixed number, independent of n, y and rho.
3. The cutoff. Fix n, y in R^n and rho > 0, and put eta(x) := psi(||x - y||^2 / rho^2). The map x -> ||x - y||^2 is C^infinity, since it is the squared Euclidean norm composed with a translation. Dividing by the constant rho^2 > 0 keeps it smooth. So eta, a C^1 function of a smooth map, is C^1 on R^n. By step 1, 0 <= eta(x) <= 1 for every x.
4. eta = 1 on B_rho(y). If ||x - y|| < rho, then ||x - y||^2 < rho^2, so ||x - y||^2 / rho^2 < 1 and eta(x) = 1 by step 1.
5. Support. Suppose eta(x) != 0. Then ||x - y||^2 / rho^2 < 3 by step 1, so ||x - y||^2 < 3 rho^2. If ||x - y|| > (7/4) rho we would have ||x - y||^2 > (49/16) rho^2 >= 3 rho^2, a contradiction. Hence ||x - y|| <= (7/4) rho, so support(eta) is contained in closedBall(y, 7 rho / 4). The closed ball is closed, so tsupport(eta), the closure of the support, is also contained in it. Since 7 rho / 4 < 2 rho, closedBall(y, 7 rho / 4) is contained in the open ball B_{2 rho}(y). So tsupport(eta) is contained in B_{2 rho}(y). Closed balls in the finite-dimensional space R^n are compact, and tsupport(eta) is a closed subset of one. Hence tsupport(eta) is compact, i.e. eta has compact support.
6. Derivative. Fix x and put s := ||x - y||^2 / rho^2. The map x' -> ||x' - y||^2 has derivative h -> 2 <x - y, h> at x. Hence x' -> ||x' - y||^2 / rho^2 has derivative ell_x := (2 / rho^2) <x - y, .>. As a linear form on R^n, ell_x has operator norm (2 / rho^2) ||x - y||, because the form <v, .> has norm ||v|| (innerSL_apply_norm). By the chain rule (HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt), D eta(x) = psi'(s) ell_x, so ||D eta(x)|| = |psi'(s)| (2 / rho^2) ||x - y||.
(a) If s > 3, then psi'(s) = 0 by step 2, so D eta(x) = 0 and ||D eta(x)|| = 0 <= K / rho.
(b) If s <= 3, then ||x - y||^2 <= 3 rho^2 <= 4 rho^2, so ||x - y|| <= 2 rho. With |psi'(s)| <= c_psi this gives ||D eta(x)|| <= c_psi (2 / rho^2) (2 rho) = 4 c_psi / rho = K / rho.
The parent proof argues the same way using ||x - y|| <= sqrt(3) rho, which gives 2 sqrt(3) c_psi / rho <= 4 c_psi / rho; the bound here is identical.
7. Conclusion. K = 4 c_psi >= 0 does not depend on n, y or rho. For every n, y and rho > 0, the function eta of step 3 is C^1, satisfies 0 <= eta <= 1, equals 1 on B_rho(y), has compact support with tsupport(eta) contained in B_{2 rho}(y), and satisfies ||D eta(x)|| <= K / rho for all x. QED

proof_key_steps: profile psi(s) = smoothTransition((3 - s)/2): C^1 with values in [0,1], psi = 1 for s <= 1, psi = 0 for s >= 3
psi' is continuous and vanishes outside [1,3], so |psi'| <= c_psi everywhere; K := 4 c_psi >= 0
eta(x) = psi(||x - y||^2/rho^2) is C^1, 0 <= eta <= 1, and eta = 1 on B_rho(y)
eta(x) != 0 implies ||x - y|| < 7 rho/4, so tsupport eta lies in closedBall(y, 7 rho/4), which is compact and inside B_{2 rho}(y)
chain rule: ||D eta(x)|| = |psi'(s)| (2/rho^2) ||x - y||; this is 0 if s > 3 and at most c_psi (2/rho^2)(2 rho) = K/rho if s <= 3
